abstract: we study black holes in gabadadze's weakly coupled effective theory of the gravitational trace anomaly, keeping both the euler and the weyl central charges. we prove that a constant anomalyon on any ricci-flat geometry, the kerr family included, solves the full theory if and only if the two central charges coincide. otherwise, the black holes continuously connected to this branch carry scalar hair whose charge is fixed by the surface gravity, the horizon topology and the difference of central charges alone: maximally supersymmetric matter leaves black holes bald, the standard model and photon-dominated sectors produce hair of definite sign, and conformal collider bounds confine it to a universal window. electric charge separates the two anomaly invariants: the hair reverses sign at a critical charge-to-mass ratio set by the ratio of central charges, its extremal value retains only the weyl charge, and the euler charge governs the near-horizon growth of the anomalyon. for every unitary matter sector, the hair regular at the event horizon diverges at the cauchy horizon. finally, once the higher-derivative weyl operator is order-reduced, the background, the anomalyon-graviton mixing and all propagation speeds depend only on the difference of central charges, which extends the no-ghost and laplacian stability conditions to the full anomaly.

title: lyapunov stability of a schwarzschild black hole surrounded by the kiselev anisotropic fluid
abstract: we investigate the geodesic structure and the stability of circular orbits around a schwarzschild black hole surrounded by a kiselev anisotropic fluid, characterised by the equation-of-state parameter $ω$ and the normalisation parameter $n$. we consider six representative values, $ω=-1,-2/3,-1/3,0,1/3$ and $1$, over the admissible range of $n$ determined by the horizon structure, including the corresponding extremal limits. using the effective potentials for null and timelike geodesics, we determine the photon sphere, the innermost stable circular orbit (isco) and the outermost stable circular orbit (osco), and examine their stability through coordinate-time lyapunov exponents. the photon sphere is unstable for all values of $ω$ and $n$ considered. its instability weakens with increasing $n$ for $ω\leq0$ and vanishes at extremality for $ω=-1$ and $-2/3$, whereas it varies non-monotonically with $n$ for $ω=1/3$ and strengthens for $ω=1$. for $ω=-1$ and $-2/3$, stable circular orbits are confined between the isco and the osco, which merge at a critical value of $n$ beyond which no stable circular orbits exist. in contrast, for $ω\geq-1/3$ stable circular orbits exist at all radii beyond the isco, whose location varies with $n$. we also derive a closed-form expression for the squared coordinate-time lyapunov exponent $(λ_t^t)^2$, valid for arbitrary $ω$, whose sign changes exactly at the isco and osco, so that the lyapunov criterion reproduces the boundaries of stable circular motion. the schwarzschild--de sitter, mass-shifted schwarzschild and reissner--nordström geometries are recovered as special cases, and the results may have implications for black-hole shadows, thin accretion discs and quasi-periodic oscillations.

title: relativistic dynamical friction and accretion for kerr black holes
abstract: extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (emris) observed by lisa will probe the environments of massive black holes (bhs), including the dark matter (dm) overdensities expected to form around them. we compute the relativistic dynamical friction and accretion experienced by a non-spinning compact object on circular equatorial orbits around a kerr bh embedded in a collisionless dm distribution, extending previous results in schwarzschild. the dm is modeled as a spike grown adiabatically from an initial hernquist profile, and the momentum transfer is obtained by integrating relativistic scattering and capture cross sections over the full, generically anisotropic phase space seen by the secondary. far from the primary the friction tracks the local dm density, which increases with spin. near the innermost stable circular orbit of rapidly spinning bhs $(a\gtrsim 0.37)$, however, frame dragging forces bound dm particles to co-rotate, so that the secondary is overtaken by the surrounding medium: the friction weakens and eventually reverses sign where the dm density peaks. we show that a similar reversal can be mimicked around a non-rotating bh if the initial halo carries large net angular momentum, although this requires anisotropies beyond those found in cosmological simulations. we also show that commonly used chandrasekhar-like prescriptions, which depend only on the local density, can overestimate the friction force. our results demonstrate that the full phase-space structure of the environment must be included when modeling dm effects on emris.

title: near-boundary and near-horizon momentum--krylov response in noncommutative-inspired btz spacetime
abstract: we compute the proper radial momentum of a massive probe falling into a lorentzian-smeared, noncommutative-inspired btz black hole at fixed asymptotic mass, and use it as the growth rate of momentum--krylov complexity. in the btz limit the accumulated complexity is $\mathcal{k}_0 = x(\coshτ- 1)$. with smearing, the initial growth coefficient is $f'_α(x)/4$, while the late-time exponent is the surface gravity $f'_α(x_+)/2$. the two depend differently on the smearing parameter, so the deformed response is not a rescaled btz curve; we show this analytically and confirm it numerically. for a distant release point the early response approaches btz, whereas the late-time rate does not. a btz black hole with the same hawking temperature reproduces the response to within about ten percent, and the remaining difference is set by the early/late mismatch. a gaussian mass profile gives the same picture. the horizon radius and the surface gravity vanish at the critical smearing with exponents $1/2$ and $3/2$. at fixed mass the boundary stress tensor coincides with that of btz, but the $z^3$ fefferman--graham coefficient and the lengths of boundary-anchored geodesics do not.

title: optimal statistic for a stochastic gravitational wave background using pulsar-timing--astrometry cross correlations
abstract: astrometric measurements have emerged as a viable probe of gravitational waves (gws), complementing pulsar timing searches by providing overlapping and higher gw frequency coverage. at its core, the search for gws using astrometry is very similar to the search with pulsar timing data: gws induce a change in pulse arrival times along the line of sight to a pulsar and a transverse angular deflection in the apparent position of a star. in analogy to pulsar timing, we develop a correlation statistic between pairs of stellar deflections for astrometry to search for a stochastic gw background. with a common formalism for both astrometry and pulsar timing, we also develop the cross-correlation statistic between stellar deflections and pulsar timing residuals. we estimate the signal-to-noise ratios from the correlation statistics and provide scaling laws in the weak- and intermediate-signal regimes.

title: on the existence of constants of motion for multipolar test-body dynamics
abstract: we show that the conservative equations of motion of an extended test body, with force and torque sourced by spin-induced and adiabatic tidal multipoles of arbitrary order, are the flow of the hamiltonian $h=-\tfrac12μ^2+μu$, where $μ$ is the body's kinematic mass and all multipoles enter through a covariant scalar potential $u$. for such bodies, a certain notion of mass and a spin norm are shown to be exactly conserved, at all multipolar orders and in any background. we then apply our framework to the kerr spacetime, and construct extensions of the carter and rüdiger constants through hexadecapolar order (quartic in spin). they are found to exist if, and only if, the body's multipoles are those of a kerr black hole. together with the energy and angular momentum, they make the dynamics of a spinning test black hole in kerr perturbatively integrable through that order. lastly, at the next, quintic-in-spin order, an analytic criterion implemented numerically reveals that neither constant admits a continuation, for any conservative multipoles. in the conservative, test-body limit, black-hole binaries thus carry a dynamical hidden symmetry shared by no other compact objects, which persists to high multipolar order but ultimately breaks.

title: free hyperboloidal evolution in 3d: gauge waves and constraint-violating gravitational waves
abstract: hyperboloidal evolution allows to reach future null infinity within numerical relativity simulations. this work extends the conformal compactification approach with bssn/z4 from spherical symmetry to full 3d simulations. this is the first free numerical hyperboloidal evolution in 3d with a common formulation of general relativity. in this first step, gauge waves and constraint-violating gravitational waves perturbing minkowski spacetime are evolved nonlinearly and show that the implementation is reliable and signals can be successfully extracted at future null infinity.

title: the schwarzschild-kerr crossover of high overtone quasinormal modes
abstract: a slowly rotating black hole is close to a nonrotating one, but its highly damped quasinormal spectrum is not. the schwarzschild approximation holds only up to overtone numbers of order $χ^{-4/3}$, where $χ$ is the dimensionless spin. we find that the frequency shift at this scale is a universal function, derived from the wave boundary conditions with an error estimate. it is given by the spectrum of a sextic oscillator, via the correspondence between ordinary differential equations and integrable models. it recovers the schwarzschild $\log 3$ and organizes the singular kerr coefficients.

title: area-minimizing surfaces and the rigidity of three-dimensional electrostatic systems
abstract: we study three-dimensional electrostatic systems, the riemannian data of static solutions of the einstein--maxwell equations with cosmological constant $λ$, by means of locally area-minimizing surfaces. such a surface with non-empty boundary on the horizons is a totally geodesic hemisphere and forces the de sitter system. a closed one in the interior forces a system of product type, one of eight models if the scalar curvature is somewhere positive on it, among them the bertotti--robinson, nariai and cold and ultracold black hole systems. no compactness, asymptotic or pinching assumption is needed. in particular, closed systems without horizons are flat or compact quotients of the nariai--bertotti--robinson system. for compact systems with connected horizon, the electric field vanishes even when the system is not simply connected, and the area of the horizon is either $12π/λ$, for de sitter, or at most $4π/λ$. with several horizons, every horizon whose area does not exceed the sum of the others is stable, minimizes area in its homology class and satisfies an area--charge inequality, with equality only for the charged nariai systems; its charged hawking mass and charge therefore lie in the parameter region of the reissner--nordström--de sitter black holes. compact systems with horizons are spherical space forms with balls removed. noncompact systems with strictly mean-convex ends have one end, and their horizons are stable and $π_1$-injective and satisfy a strict area--charge inequality.

title: dec fill-ins, the bartnik--bray inner mass, and positive mass theorems with untrapped boundary
abstract: given a closed $(n-1)$-dimensional manifold equipped with prescribed spacetime bartnik data, we ask when this can be realised as the boundary of a compact $n$-dimensional initial data set satisfying the dominant energy condition (dec). this is a natural generalisation of the problem of non-negative scalar curvature fill-ins, where the boundary metric and mean curvature are prescribed. we give conditions on the bartnik data that suffice to prove the existence of such dec fill-ins with inner mots boundary, and give some applications of these fill-ins.   our first application of these is a lower bound on the bartnik--bray inner mass, which we slightly reformulate here to be a genuine spacetime definition. our other applications include proving a positive mass theorem for spin initial data with boundary that need not be trapped, and a spacetime penrose-like inequality that gives a positive lower bound on the mass of an initial data set with boundary in terms of its boundary bartnik data assuming the spacetime penrose inequality holds.

title: classification of solutions to the energy-critical complex ginzburg-landau equation and application to nls
abstract: for the energy-critical complex ginzburg--landau equation, we establish a dichotomy between global existence and finite-time blow-up below the ground-state energy. at the threshold energy, we classify solutions and describe their dynamics in terms of the \(\dot h^1\) norm of the initial data relative to that of the ground state.   these results and their application to energy-critical focusing nonlinear schrödinger equations extend our previous work [j. math. pures appl., 2026] to all dimensions \(d\ge3\) and to the ground-state energy threshold.   furthermore, we strengthen the weak--strong uniqueness result for the focusing nls by removing the additional smallness assumption imposed in our previous work.

title: well-posedness of the hodge wave equation on a compact manifold
abstract: in this work, we study the hodge wave equation on a compact orientable manifold. we present the necessary differential geometry language to treat sobolev spaces of differential forms and use these tools to identify a boundary triplet for the problem.   we use this boundary triplet to determine a class of boundary conditions for which the problem is well-posed.

title: transmission and reflection coefficients for schrödinger operators with truncated periodic potentials that support defect states
abstract: we consider scattering waves through truncated periodic potentials with perturbations that support localized gap eigenstates. in a small complex neighborhood around an assumed positive bound state of the model operator, we prove the existence of a distinct zero reflection state, or transmission resonance. we compare its location to a previously found scattering resonance and use the properties of solutions near these interesting points to analyze the behavior of transmission and reflection coefficients of scattering solutions near the assumed bound state. by example, we also discuss the truncated simple harmonic oscillator and compare the analysis to the crystalline case.

title: direct scattering of the focusing nonlinear schrödinger equation with step-like oscillatory initial data
abstract: in this manuscript we set up the direct and inverse scattering problems for step-like traveling wave solutions of the nonlinear schrödinger equation. specifically, we consider the initial data $u_0(x)=u_e^\ell(x)$ for $x<0$ and $u_0(x)=u_e^r(x)$ for $x>0$, where $u_e^\ell(x)$ and $u_e^r(x)$ are elliptic traveling wave solutions of nls. more generally, we consider initial data satisfying $u_0(x)\to u_e^\ell(x)$ as $x\to-\infty$ and $u_0(x)\to u_e^r(x)$ as $x\to+\infty$. under the assumption that $u_0-u_e^\ell \in l^{1,2}(\mathbb{r}^-)$ and $u_0-u_e^r \in l^{1,2}(\mathbb{r}^+)$, we formulate the direct scattering problem and establish analytic properties of the scattering data. we then formulate the inverse problem as a riemann--hilbert problem and prove its solvability, thus proving the existence of the nonlinear schrödinger solution with the above step-like initial data. finally, we observe that our riemann--hilbert formulation is a special case of the one arising for full soliton-gas initial data.

title: local reynolds number criteria for the regularity of the three-dimensional navier-stokes equations, and their consistency with forced finite-time blow-up
abstract: we give four regularity criteria for the forced navier-stokes equations in $\mathbb{r}^3$. the first is an $\dot h^1$ estimate: a strong solution cannot blow up while the local reynolds number $|v|^2/(ν|ω|)$ stays below $4/(3\sqrt3)$ wherever the vorticity exceeds a threshold $m(t)$ with $\int m^{6/5}\,dt<\infty$. it rests on an exact identity that gives the cubic vorticity term a favorable sign. two further $\dot h^1$ estimates use the newton potential of $|ω|^2$, either as a multiplier or as a gradient added to the lamb vector, so that the integral of $|ω|^2|v|^2$ cancels. the second of these gives a critical condition on the vorticity alone, implied by $\int\|ω\|_{l^3}^2\,dt<\infty$. the fourth is a maximum principle for $\frac12|v|^2+λ|ω|$: vortex stretching is absorbed by viscous dissipation, and the pressure is controlled by a weighted local estimate. it requires a bound on $|v|^2/(ν|\nabla v|)$ only at maximum points where the velocity part dominates. we show that the forced finite-time blow-up recently constructed by openai violates each hypothesis, and that the violations locate its mechanism: inflow down the centripetal pressure gradient, at the same order as viscous dissipation.

title: a mixed-primal fem for poisson-fermi interfacial problems
abstract: this paper presents a mixed-primal fem for a linearised poisson--fermi interface problem arising from the bazant--storey--kornyshev theory, which describes electrostatic interactions in ionic solutions. it leads to a transmission problem coupling a fourth-order equation in the solvent region with a second-order equation in the solute region. to precisely compute the electrostatic stress and the interactive force in the electrolyte, we reformulate the fourth-order problem as a mixed system by introducing the gradient of the electrostatic potential, the divergence of its gradient, and the gradient of its divergence as additional independent variables. the second-order problem is studied in its primal form as this approach eliminates the requirement for lagrange multipliers to enforce the transmission conditions. the resulting formulation is discretised using raviart--thomas finite elements for the vector variables and piecewise polynomial finite elements for the scalar variables. well-posedness of the mixed-primal formulation and optimal a priori error estimates for the field variables as well as for the postprocessed maxwell tensor are established under suitable regularity assumptions, in parameter-weighted norms in which the inf-sup constant is independent of the correlation length and of the permittivity ratio. the constants in the error estimates are independent of both parameters as well, up to a loss of at most half an order when the mesh does not resolve the length scale (square root of the relative permittivity); the sobolev norms of the solution may still depend on the parameters through boundary layers. the postprocessed maxwell stress converges with optimal order on quasi-uniform meshes, except for the lowest-order scheme in 3d. numerical experiments validate the theoretical convergence rates and demonstrate the properties of the proposed method for problems in 2d and 3d.

title: modified wave operators for the critical long-range nonlinear schrödinger equation
abstract: in this paper, we construct modified wave operators for the critical long-range nonlinear schrödinger equation with final data $\langle x\rangle^s u_+\in l_x^2,\ d/2<s\le2$, for dimensions $d=1,2,3$, and for both defocusing and focusing cases. we impose no smallness, nonvanishing, or spatial derivative assumption. most previous modified wave operator results require smallness on $\|\widehat u_+\|_{l^\infty}$, analytic final data or smooth amplitude-phase structure, and the large data modified wave operator problem with finite weighted condition is only solved for 1d defocusing equation.   we introduce a new perturbation method which successfully applies to both defocusing and focusing signs when $d\le3$. the main ingredient is an improved growth estimate for the linearized flow, obtained by a low--high frequency decomposition. at low frequencies, spatial localization and freezing the coefficients in space lead to a fuchsian system. the nilpotent structure at the singular point and a hamiltonian energy estimate give logarithmic growth for this system. at high frequencies, a modified energy for suitable symmetry operator cancels the leading contribution to energy growth.

title: upwind finite element approximation of the gradient blow-up time for a viscous hamilton--jacobi equation
abstract: we analyze an upwind finite element method with piecewise linear elements for a viscous hamilton--jacobi equation with a superquadratic gradient source term, subject to homogeneous dirichlet boundary conditions. on polytopal inner approximations of smooth bounded domains in dimensions $n=1,2,3$, we prove maximum-norm convergence of the numerical solution to the exact solution before gradient blow-up and convergence of gradient-threshold times to the blow-up time under explicit mesh and regularity assumptions. we also verify the regularity assumption and finite-time gradient blow-up for an example on the disk, to which the main theorem therefore applies. numerical experiments illustrate this gradient blow-up.

title: weighted pointwise estimates for the damped wave equation and global solutions to nakao's problem in three dimensions
abstract: in this paper, we establish weighted pointwise estimates for the duhamel term of the three-dimensional damped wave equation. the estimates combine the parabolic weight $\langle t+|x|^2\rangle$ with the wave-cone weight $\langle t-|x|\rangle$, and thereby account for both the diffusive part of the damped wave flow and source terms with wave-like decay. as an application, we study nakao's problem, a weakly coupled system consisting of one semilinear damped wave equation and one semilinear wave equation. under explicit conditions on the exponents of nonlinear terms, we prove small-data global existence and uniqueness of mild solutions in weighted $l^\infty$ spaces. the result covers both the full parabolic decay and slower pointwise decay for the damped-wave component, and allows either the standard wave decay or slower pointwise decay for the wave component. the proof combines the new duhamel estimate with weighted estimates for the free wave equation and a contraction argument.

title: observable sets for one-dimensional schrödinger equations with subquadratic power potentials
abstract: in this paper, we study observability inequalities for the one-dimensional schrödinger equation associated with the operator $h_m=-\partial_x^2+|x|^{2m}$, where $0<m\leq1$. for $0<m<1/2$, observability in some positive time, and equivalently in every positive time, is characterized by the thickness of the observation set. this extends the characterization of chen--liu--liu at $m=1/2$. for $1/2<m\leq1$, we characterize observable sets in terms of the asymptotic lower density on the spatial intervals $i_{m,a}(x)=[x-a|x|^{2m-1},x+a|x|^{2m-1}]$. observability in some positive time is equivalent to positive density at some scale, whereas observability in every positive time is equivalent to positive density at every scale. moreover, for $1/2<m<1$, the minimal observation time is comparable to the square root of the critical density scale.

title: exact solutions and a critical-damping threshold for a nonlinear transport-wave equation
abstract: linear stability theory does not determine whether a small disturbance in a physical system decays or grows without bound when the disturbance has finite size and the damping varies in time. we address this question for the nonlinear damped transport-wave equation $u_{tt}+cu_{xt}+γu_t=λu(u_t+cu_x)e^{-γt}$, a constant-coefficient case of a model introduced in previous work. combining the method of characteristics with a riccati reduction, we reduce the equation exactly to a first-order ordinary differential equation at each point and solve it explicitly. for a natural class of initial data, the solution has a critical damping rate $\gc$, given in closed form in terms of the initial data: for $γ<\gc$ the solution blows up in finite time, and otherwise no finite-time singularity occurs. a similar result holds for time-dependent damping and for power-law feedback. applications to shock formation in the damped burgers equation, gelation with decaying reactivity and frictional heating under a moving band are presented.

title: on the number of positive solutions of the nonlinear schrödinger equation on compact star graphs
abstract: in this paper, we consider the number and the shape of positive solutions of the nonlinear schrödinger equation on compact symmetric star graphs with dirichlet condition at the exterior vertex and kirchhoff condition at the central vertex.

title: finite-time blowup in the inviscid goy and sabra models
abstract: for the inviscid goy and sabra shell models with zero boundary conditions at the lowest shells, we construct strong solutions with finitely supported initial data whose vorticity amplitudes blow up in the supremum norm in finite time, at the self-similar rate $(t-t)^{-1}$. the blowup is stable under small perturbations of the initial data in the same norm, including complex-valued ones.   guided by the work of mailybaev, we use a travelling wave of the renormalized equations to obtain blowup in the original variables. we construct such a wave for the equations extended to all integer shells, decaying in both directions. we then show that the dynamics near this wave contract once the directions generated by time-translation and phase symmetries are removed by adjusting the symmetry parameters at each step (a modulation argument). this yields blowup solutions on the positive shells satisfying the original boundary conditions. computer-assisted interval arithmetic is used to establish the existence of the travelling wave and the contraction estimate needed for the modulation argument.

title: low-regularity evolution and control for the nonlinear schrödinger equation with singular bilinear interactions
abstract: we consider the one-dimensional nonlinear schrödinger equation (nls) $i\dt ψ-\dx^2 ψ= (u(t)\cdot μ) ψ+κ|ψ|^{2m}ψ,$ on the torus under the presence of singular, time-dependent bilinear external fields $(u(t)\cdot μ)$. we prove well-posedness in $h^s(\t)$ for low regularity indices $s>\max\big\{\tfrac12-\tfrac1m,0\big\}$ ($s>0$ when $κ=0$), under sharp assumptions on the singular potentials, covering both the linear and nonlinear cases. we establish small-time exact controllability in $h^{\frac12+}(\t)$ for a large class of states, by combining saturation techniques with the moment method. the result extends previous bilinear exact controllability results for linear schrödinger equations, which are typically obtained in large time and under high regularity assumptions. crucial to our approach is the role of the singular time-dependent potentials, which enable the recovery of controllability properties in small time and at low regularity, overcoming obstructions present in the smooth setting.

title: investigating tidal heating in neutron stars via gravitational raman scattering
abstract: we present a scattering amplitude formalism to study the tidal heating effects of nonspinning neutron stars incorporating both worldline effective field theory and relativistic stellar perturbation theory. in neutron stars, tidal heating arises from fluid viscosity due to various scattering processes in the interior. it also serves as a channel for the exchange of energy and angular momentum between the neutron star and its environment. in the interior of the neutron star, we first derive two master perturbation equations that capture fluid perturbations accurate to linear order in frequency. remarkably, these equations receive no contribution from bulk viscosity due to a peculiar adiabatic incompressibility which arises in stellar fluid for non-barotropic perturbations. in the exterior, the metric perturbations reduce to the regge-wheeler (rw) equation which we solve using the analytical mano-suzuki-takasugi (mst) method. we compute the amplitude for gravitational waves scattering off a neutron star, also known as gravitational raman scattering. from the amplitude, we obtain expressions for the electric quadrupolar static love number and the leading dissipation number to all orders in compactness. we then compute the leading dissipation number for various realistic equation-of-state(s) and estimate the change in the number of gravitational wave cycles due to tidal heating during inspiral in the ligo-virgo-kagra (lvk) band. we find that the shear-viscous contribution is small. even for cold ($t\sim 10^5$k) and weakly compact stars it changes the number of cycles by less than $10^{-2}$, about an order of magnitude below the other conservative 4pn contributions, and it decreases as $t^{-2}$ for hotter stars.

title: influence of perfect fluid dark matter on shadow observables of yang-mills modified charged black holes
abstract: we investigate the influence of perfect fluid dark matter (pfdm) on yang--mills--inspired charged black holes, with a particular focus on the resulting modifications to key black hole observables. by embedding a pfdm term into the spacetime geometry, we examine the alterations in shadow morphology, photon geodesics, and the associated energy emission spectra. our analysis reveals that pfdm induces notable deviations in the shadow size, shape, and circularity, and significantly impacts the stability of circular orbits. furthermore, the energy emission rate exhibits a strong dependence on both the yang--mills charge and the dark matter distribution. these results indicate that environmental effects arising from dark matter can imprint observable signatures on black hole shadows and radiation processes, offering a potential pathway to constrain dark matter models and probe non-kerr geometries with forthcoming high-precision observations such as those from the event horizon telescope and next-generation interferometers.

title: prospect on constraining environment-dependent dilaton model from gravitational redshift measurements
abstract: scalar-tensor gravity represents a natural extension of general relativity. this paper investigates the prospects for constraining the environmentally dependent dilaton through atomic-clock comparisons across media of different densities. using the scalar compton wavelength, we assess how the finite size of the surrounding medium and screening by the clock enclosure limit the accessible region. to test the continuous-density approximation for dilute media, we model matter as a periodic lattice of spherical particles and compare an analytic neumann solution with a three-dimensional finite-element solution on the cubic box. the continuous and discrete models give indistinguishable redshift predictions near the $10^{-20}$ and $10^{-25}$ benchmarks. in the strong-coupling regime, differences become apparent on redshift contours of order $10^{-46}$ or lower. under the assumed environmental and instrumental conditions, comparisons involving a dense medium identify a window for probing smaller values of $a_2$, offering a gravitational-redshift test complementary to existing fifth-force searches.

title: spiral density waves and torque balance in the kerr geometry
abstract: extreme mass-ratio inspirals (emris) in relativistic accretion discs are a key science target for the upcoming lisa mission. existing models of disc-emri interactions typically rely on crude dynamical friction or newtonian planetary migration prescriptions, which fail to capture the relativistic fluid response induced by the binary potential. in this work we address this gap by providing the relativistic calculation. we apply standard methods from self-force theory, black hole perturbation theory, and relativistic stellar perturbation theory to compute the relativistic analogue of the spiral density wave and torque-balance results underlying planetary migration. specifically, we calculate the response of a perfect fluid disc to the perturbing potential of an emri, consistently incorporating pressure effects. using a master enthalpy-like variable and linearised fluid theory, we present a set of proof-of-principle calculations that reconstruct the fluid perturbations and relativistic spiral arm structure for a range of spin values in the kerr geometry. we derive a relativistic torque-balance equation that enables us to compute and compare local torques with the angular momentum advected through the disc, finding striking agreement when applied to our relativistic disc-emri solutions. this opens a promising route towards establishing torque-balance relations between integrated disc torques arising from fluid perturbations and the forces acting on emris embedded in matter.

title: memory effect for generalized modes in pp-wave spacetimes
abstract: the memory effect of test particles interacting with pp-wave gaussian pulses is investigated for { higher-order polynomial pp--wave modes beyond the standard quadrupolar $+$ and $\times$ profiles}. massive geodesic equations are solved numerically for several values of the { polynomial index $m$}, allowing the analysis of velocity and energy memory effects. in order to eliminate possible coordinate artifacts, the study is formulated in terms of the relative motion between two test particles. the results show that the relative kinetic energy variation exhibits a quartic dependence on the wave amplitude in the regime of low initial velocities. the coefficient of this scaling is found to depend on the { transverse polynomial structure of the wave, reflecting the spatial gradients associated with the different modes}. it is further shown that the energy memory effect is determined by the integrated tidal field, linking the permanent change in the relative kinetic energy to the history of the spacetime curvature carried by the wave.

title: quark stars in $f(t,\mathcal{t}) $ gravity: structure, stability, and observational constraints
abstract: quark stars-hypothetical compact stars made entirely of deconfined quark matter-offer a clean testing ground for gravity beyond general relativity. we study their structure in $f(t,\mathcal{t})$ gravity, a teleparallel theory in which torsion is coupled directly to the trace of the energy-momentum tensor through a single constant coupling. using the standard mit bag description of quark matter, we solve the modified stellar structure equations and follow how the mass, radius, compactness, and surface redshift respond as the coupling is varied across its full admissible range. the maximum mass turns out to depend on the coupling in a non-monotonic way: it rises above the general relativity value, peaks near 2.02 solar masses at a moderate positive coupling, and then falls steeply as the coupling approaches a critical value at which the structure equations become singular. the two-solar-mass pulsar constraint is satisfied within a finite window of positive couplings. all configurations on the candidate stable branch satisfy causality and remain below the standard general-relativistic compactness and surface-redshift benchmarks.

title: magnetic catalysis and fermion mass generation in de sitter spacetime
abstract: we consider the dynamics of a charged fermion in de sitter space in the presence of a uniform background magnetic field, and discuss magnetic catalysis of chiral symmetry breaking using the nambu--jona-lasinio (njl) model. we evaluate the mode functions of the charged fermion field in this background by imposing the bunch--davies vacuum condition. the gap equation is solved in the mean-field approximation. we derive analytic expressions for the gap in several limiting regimes, such as the large-magnetic-field and large-curvature limits. we find that the curvature effect restores chiral symmetry, whereas the magnetic field enhances chiral symmetry breaking through the conventional mechanism of magnetic catalysis. the phase structure associated with chiral symmetry breaking is revealed by numerical calculations.

title: c-infinity compact-support wormholes with exact schwarzschild exterior in trace-coupled gravity
abstract: we construct static, spherically symmetric wormholes in trace-coupled gravity with $f(r,t)=r+λt^2$. smooth deformations of schwarzschild vanish to all orders outside a finite core, producing an exact schwarzschild exterior without a thin shell. under two explicitly assumed anisotropic-fluid closures, the matter reconstruction reduces to a cubic equation for $χ=λt/(4π)$. the vacuum boundary selects a locally unique root; its simple continuation must remain separate from the singular inversion surface. we distinguish root folds from vanishing $1+χ$ and terminate numerical continuation when the selected root coalesces. regular examples have either positive or negative throat density. on every regular branch the physical radial null energy condition fails at the throat; for the undeformed-redshift family it fails throughout the open core. the nonvacuum sector has finite support, whereas the exterior retains the schwarzschild weyl field and mass $m$. reproducible phase maps, convergence tests, and high-precision tail checks support these conditional existence results. no dynamical stability or microphysical matter model is asserted.

title: sourced stationary dirac bound states around kerr black holes
abstract: ultralight bosonic fields can form macroscopic clouds around rotating black holes, whereas the existence of analogous stationary fermionic configurations is constrained by their intrinsic spin. here we study stationary bound states of massive dirac fields supported by an external source on kerr backgrounds, in the test-field approximation, with a kinematic extension to kerr--newman, they are not fermionic condensates in the many-body sense. by mapping the kerr--dirac system to a globally integrated sourced radial problem, we isolate the boundary constraints dictated by horizon causality. the angular sector shows that for $|m|=1/2$ the regular boundary branches prevent the field density from vanishing on the rotation axis, whereas modes with $|m|\ge3/2$ vanish there, the reconstructed kerr density is only mildly oblate. precisely at the kinematic synchronization locus, the frobenius matrix of the dirac operator is non-defective and devoid of logarithmic divergences. regularity on the future horizon nevertheless selects the ingoing solution, and an exact radial flux identity shows that this solution carries a positive flux, which excludes source-free normalizable states at all frequencies. the exclusion of source-free synchronized states demonstrates that a black hole's capacity to support macroscopic stationary fields is governed not merely by superradiant kinematics, but by the interplay between horizon regularity and the positivity of the dirac flux.

title: tidally induced coda: double transients from black hole-star binary encounters with massive black holes
abstract: dense stellar environments surrounding massive black holes (mbhs) provide a natural setting for dynamical interactions that can produce transient electromagnetic and gravitational-wave sources. in particular, the tidal field of an mbh can strongly perturb binaries undergoing close encounters with it, driving their internal orbits to extreme eccentricities. here, we investigate the outcomes of such interactions for binaries composed of a stellar-mass black hole (bh) and a star. using direct few-body scattering experiments with the code spacehub, we explore hyperbolic encounters between bh-star binaries and mbhs. we systematically quantify the probabilities of different dynamical outcomes as functions of the binary orbital parameters and mbh mass, with particular emphasis on a channel in which the tidally induced eccentricity triggers a micro-tidal disruption event ($μ$tde), as the star is disrupted by its bh companion, followed by accretion of the stellar debris onto the mbh. we derive fitting formulae for the $μ$tde cross section and for the time delay between the two resulting flares, finding that the latter can be a few months for an mbh of $10^6\,m_\odot$. these double transients offer a distinctive observational signature of $μ$tdes. we estimate event rates ranging from a few to $\sim 100\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$ within a luminosity distance of $40\,{\rm gpc}$.

title: late-time cosmic acceleration from matter inhomogeneities: constraints from desi dr2 and sne ia
abstract: we present the first observational constraints on the misner-sharp (ms) mass of the universe, within a newly proposed exact general relativity solution providing a non-perturbative description of nonlinear cosmic structure formation. at early times, when statistical homogeneity and isotropy are satisfied, our model reduces to usual flrw cosmology, accommodating cosmic microwave background (cmb) data. at late times, the departure from homogeneity and isotropy on scales $\lesssim 200$ mpc -- codified in the scale-dependent redshift distribution of the ms mass -- naturally induces cosmic acceleration, through an extensive term generated by the ms mass asymptotic limit on large scales. we derive the ms mass from baryon acoustic oscillation data from the dark energy spectroscopic instrument (desi) and type ia supernovae, obtaining a value of the cosmological constant in agreement with $λ$cdm results. we outline broader implications and future observational prospects, highlighting how multi-probe strategies -- particularly cmb lensing and the late integrated sachs-wolfe effect -- can ultimately test this solution to the dark energy puzzle.

title: a kerr-black-hole worldline action to $\mathcal{o}(g^5)$
abstract: we establish a worldline action which correctly reproduces kerr-black-hole dynamics up to fifth order in newton's constant in a physical post-minkowskian counting. this encompasses operators up to second order in the riemann curvature tensor and up to fourth order in the spin tensor. doing so entails performing the full effective-field-theory computation of the amplitude for a gravitational-wave scattering off of a spinning compact object up to four-loop order, and matching the result to the predictions from linear black hole perturbation theory. quadratic-in-curvature operators which must be added to match successfully include time-reversal anti-symmetric ones at linear and cubic spin orders, capturing absorption across the black hole horizon, and conservative quadratic-in-spin ones. as an immediate application of our action, we compute the leading-order change in spin magnitude, and reproduce the leading change in mass, for a kerr black hole in a scattering event with a second compact body, considering a generic orientation of the black hole's spin.

title: how to play a black hole: understanding quasinormal mode excitation
abstract: understanding the excitation of black hole quasinormal modes is essential for interpreting gravitational-wave signals and inferring black hole properties from them. in this work, we investigate the excitation of the quasinormal modes of schwarzschild black holes under controlled probes. in the absence of a source, we find that broader initial data suppresses mode excitation, enhancing the relative contribution of the late-time tail, while data localized near the light ring strongly suppresses overtones relative to the fundamental mode. on the other hand, plunging sources give rise to two distinct ringdown stages, associated with scattered radiation generated during the particle's infall and with the particle crossing the light ring. finally, we investigate how much of the signal is sourced from the strong-field region by switching off the source at some finite radius. the resulting waveform is exponentially close -- in cutoff radius -- to that of a standard infall. these results provide insight into the dependence of qnm excitation on the properties and dynamics of the perturbation, and offer a controlled setting in which to investigate the origin of black hole ringdown.

title: on the evidence of lensing in gw231123
abstract: just like light, gravitational waves may be gravitationally lensed by massive objects along their travel path, however, this has not been observed so far. gw231123 is the most massive binary black-hole merger observed to-date, and quasi-circular gravitational wave analyses infer high masses and spin parameters that are particularly sensitive to the waveform model used. here we investigate whether gravitational lensing can account for these features. we model the signal as a superposition of multiple overlapping images of the same merger and find support for lensing across four waveform models. the lensing interpretation reduces the support for these high spins, bringing both the inferred spins and masses into closer agreement across waveform models. a comparison with a background of unlensed signals gives the lensing interpretation an estimated significance of $3.96^{+0.68}_{-0.30}σ$. this makes lensing a compelling interpretation of this event but is insufficient for a definitive claim.

title: split ends: uv physics branches black hole hair
abstract: coupling a shift-symmetric scalar field to the gauss-bonnet invariant modifies black holes (bhs) via scalar hair. here we consider this field to be the goldstone of a complex scalar field with a symmetry-breaking potential. for bhs of a size comparable with the inverse mass gap, the gapped field tries to restore the symmetry close to the horizon, enhancing the departure from standard bhs. moreover, bhs of the same mass can have up to three different horizon areas and surface gravities. this branching has profound consequences for bh physics, potentially observable in gravitational waves.

title: anisotropic fluid inhomogeneous cosmology
abstract: we propose a new framework for inhomogeneous cosmology based on general relativity sourced by an anisotropic fluid. the model is parametrized by a single input function, the radial misner--sharp mass distribution at different redshifts, and admits exact solutions to einstein's equations. going beyond the standard assumption of small metric perturbations, it provides a fully relativistic framework to describe the non-linear regime of cosmic structure formation. the friedmann-lemaître-robertson-walker (flrw) cosmology is recovered both at early times and -- on large scales only -- at late times. our anisotropic fluid inhomogeneous cosmology (afic) model provides a natural mechanism through which matter inhomogeneities give rise to late-time acceleration. the extensive term driving this effect does not enter the exact metric solution and therefore does not contribute to the local gravitational potential. rather, it emerges as a genuinely large-scale effect induced by the inhomogeneous distribution of matter at late times. this mechanism may provide a physical interpretation of the results from the dark energy spectroscopic instrument (desi). finally, we present a simple analytical realization of the model and use it to provide an estimate of the present-day effective dark energy density.

title: machine learning enables full bayesian inference for spinning extreme-mass-ratio inspirals
abstract: extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (emris), stellar-mass compact objects spiralling into massive black holes, promise to measure the masses and spins of the central black holes, reveal the strong-field environment around them and gauge cosmic distances via millihertz gravitational-wave observations. yet most forecasts for the parameter inference of these systems assume known source parameters, and broad-prior analyses have addressed only simplified versions of the problem. the joint inversion of all 14 parameters of a spinning source from the complete prior has remained unsolved. here we solve it for the augmented analytic kludge model: generative networks narrow the complete prior and reveal a ring of degenerate spin directions, and the exact detector likelihood determines the posterior. for a simulated one-year lisa-taiji observation, within one ring sector we obtain, for the first time, a 14-parameter posterior of a spinning emri from the complete prior, the most precise yet obtained for such a source from broad priors. the redshifted mass and spin of the massive black hole are determined to two parts in $10^5$, the mass two orders of magnitude beyond any electromagnetic measurement. the compact object's redshifted mass is measured to one part in $10^4$, and its eccentric, retrograde orbit discriminates between capture channels. the 0.8% distance and sub-square-degree localization are sufficient for dark-siren cosmology. year-long coherent analysis resolves the inspiral driven by radiation reaction itself.

title: completing the real-space construction of the canonical harmonic coordinates of kerr metric
abstract: in this paper, we determine the exact canonical harmonic kerr metric to all post-minkowskian (pm) orders within the multipolar post-minkowskian (mpm) formalism. the metric agrees with the previously constructed 4pm results. using a formal series ring, we prove that no homogeneous components of laplacian operator appear in this metric at pm order $n\ge2$. together with the equality of the linear field with the canonical kerr solution, this property allows an inductive construction of the canonical mpm metric where all gauge moments vanish. the coordinate transformation linking the canonical harmonic kerr metric to the boyer-lindquist metric is generated by the real part of a complex harmonic radial function. a recent independent construction by sadu and vanhove using momentum-space recursion and a residual homogeneous freedom classification yields the same result, providing a cross validation of the closed-form canonical harmonic kerr metric.

title: exact mass multipoles of distorted schwarzschild spacetimes
abstract: using the isolated-horizon framework, we compute the geometric and mass multipole moments of the weyl-distorted schwarzschild horizon without linearizing the distortion. starting from the exact integral representation we evaluate it in closed form for two cases, a pure quadrupole distortion and a dipole-quadrupole-octupole distortion. for a pure quadrupole we obtain a closed form for all $\ell$ in terms of confluent hypergeometric functions, while for a dipole-quadrupole-octupole distortion we derive a closed-form series solution in the odd-parity coefficient $β$ whose coefficients are exact in the quadrupole coefficient $α_{2}$. we use these results to understand the errors incurred by leading-order approximations. leading-order approximations in $α_{2}$ misestimate every dimensionless mass multipole by a relative error of roughly $α_{2}$, nearly independent of $\ell$, and for pure linearization most of the error lies in the linearized quadrupole moment rather than the discarded higher multipoles. a simple degree-counting rule determines which orders of distortion contribute to each multipole. as a consequence, the odd-parity component must be small compared with $α_{2}^2$ before it can be neglected. finally, truncating the series in $β$ at its first $β$-dependent order reproduces the $\ell \leq 6$ multipoles to about $10^{-3}$ for $|β|,|α_{2}| \leq 1/8$.

title: toward solving the galactic foreground problem in gravitational-wave astronomy with machine learning
abstract: space-borne gravitational-wave detectors will see tens of millions of galactic binaries. resolved, they would form a census of the galaxy's ultracompact binaries unhindered by dust; unresolved, they are the dominant noise up to a few millihertz for massive black-hole binaries, extreme-mass-ratio inspirals and backgrounds from the early universe. separating the two requires the number of binaries, which is ill-defined because binaries exist at every amplitude. we make it an observable by defining a source as a binary above a signal-to-noise threshold. neural flows count the binaries to within one in 99% of 1 microhertz intervals over 0.5-10 mhz, and nested sampling resolves them, even pairs closer than one frequency bin. the data themselves set a limit: a source is resolvable only if its signal pays for its own description, about 20 nats, which biases even ideal trans-dimensional samplers. like the diffraction limit in imaging, this bayesian confusion limit is set by the data rather than by the method, and it governs any superposition of weak sources, from radio surveys and pulsar timing arrays to super-resolution microscopy. for future space-borne detectors, the method turns the galactic foreground into a definite, calibrated count of binaries with an analytic selection function, the basis for global fits and for tests of population models.

title: an uncalibrated effective-one-body waveform model for intermediate-mass-ratio black hole binaries
abstract: intermediate-mass-ratio binaries, with mass ratios $q=m_1/m_2\sim10^2-10^4$, are among the most challenging sources for waveform modeling. we present an inspiral-merger-ringdown effective-one-body model for nonspinning, quasicircular binaries with $q>10$, with dynamics built only from analytical post-newtonian results. it reaches $(2,2)$ unfaithfulness of $10^{-4}-10^{-5}$ against numerical-relativity simulations with $q>10$ and subradian dephasing against second-order self-force waveforms over four-year inspirals at $q=10^4-10^5$. an optimized post-adiabatic implementation enables waveform generation up to two orders of magnitude faster than integrating the full equations of motion.

title: strong hyperbolicity of puncture-gauge formulations of gravitational theories with second order equations of motion
abstract: we prove that the modified ccz4 (mccz4) formulation, used in nonlinear puncture-gauge simulations of (d+1)-dimensional einstein-gauss-bonnet gravity and four-derivative scalar-tensor theory in four dimensions, is strongly hyperbolic for both theories at sufficiently weak coupling, provided that the gauge parameters are chosen to satisfy a cone-separation condition. the proof applies to the full principal symbol of the theories, extending previous analyses based on first-order perturbation theory about the einstein limit. we establish strong hyperbolicity by recasting the mccz4 equations into a formally equivalent second-order system whose derivative structure resembles that of the modified harmonic formulation of kovács and reall. this allows us to adapt their covariant characteristic analysis and continuity argument, without assuming that individual eigenvalues or eigenvectors depend analytically on the coupling. we also show that standard ccz4 in general relativity is strongly hyperbolic in puncture gauge away from two defective degeneracies.

title: geometrothermodynamics characterization of abg-ads black hole immersed by string clouds
abstract: regular black holes, whose singular cores are replaced by smooth geometries sourced by nonlinear electrodynamics, provide a natural setting to study how thermodynamic stability is encoded in spacetime geometry. conventional stability criteria, however, depend on the choice of thermodynamic potential. here we develop the quasi-homogeneous geometrothermodynamics of the regular ayón-beato--garcía anti-de sitter (abg-ads) black hole surrounded by a cloud of strings, a legendre-invariant framework in which no potential needs to be preferred. we show that the entropy, electric monopole charge and ads radius act as extensive variables obeying a generalized quasi-homogeneity condition, and that the equilibrium manifold then carries three families of thermodynamic metrics. we establish an exact correspondence between response-function anomalies and curvature singularities: the first metric's curvature diverges on the zero-temperature extremal boundary, where the heat capacity vanishes, signaling davies first-order transitions, whereas the second's diverges precisely where the heat capacity does, pinpointing davies second-order transitions. the gibbs free energy displays a swallow-tail structure that reveals a first-order small/large black hole transition, whose metastable region is bounded by these divergences of the heat capacity, together with a hawking--page-type transition to thermal ads. the string-cloud density and the electric charge jointly control the horizon structure, the admissible thermal domain and the stability intervals.

title: general-relativistic vlasov disks in external magnetic fields around kerr black holes
abstract: we investigate stationary general-relativistic kinetic models of a collisionless gas around the kerr black hole immersed in an external magnetic field. the main focus is put on razor-thin disks confined to the equatorial plane, but geometrically thick disks are also briefly mentioned. we consider distribution functions corresponding to constant canonical energy and constant canonical angular momentum of particles within the disk and obtain analytic expressions for the electric current associated with the gas. more general solutions characterized by distribution functions depending on the energy and the angular momentum are obtained assuming the schwarzschild background metric. in explicit examples, we investigate disks in the wald magnetosphere, describing an asymptotically uniform magnetic field.

title: scalar perturbations in extremal reissner-nordström geometry: new methods at work
abstract: we study scalar radiation emitted by a particle moving along a circular orbit around a four-dimensional extremal reissner-nordström black hole. in particular, we calculate the energy fluxes carried by scalar waves to infinity and across the event horizon, as well as the scalar self-force acting on the particle, and express all these quantities as post-newtonian expansions. our results for the energy fluxes are in agreement with previous numerical findings in the literature. to solve the radial wave equation, we employ and test two distinct analytic approaches: the first is the so-called \textit{kink method}, a novel alternative stemming from quantum integrability and the second is the mano-suzuki-takasugi method. the perfect agreement of the results highlights the potential of the kink method as a complementary tool for studying wave propagation in black-hole spacetimes.

title: sharp decay and regularity thresholds for minkowski stability in spherical symmetry
abstract: we establish sharp decay and regularity thresholds for minkowski stability in the spherically symmetric einstein--scalar field system. for small smooth characteristic data measured in weighted derivative seminorms, we prove global stability at borderline decay and half-derivative regularity of the initial data. the resulting developments remain uniformly close to minkowski spacetime and are future causally geodesically complete. both thresholds are sharp: below either the decay or regularity threshold, we construct arbitrarily small smooth, initially untrapped data whose developments contain trapped spheres.

title: gravitational collapse to extremal black holes with $λ>0$: counterexamples to the third law without charge
abstract: we study the dynamical formation of the extremal schwarzschild-de sitter solution, in both its time orientations, and the related nariai solution. we prove that there exist spherically symmetric, regular cauchy data for the einstein-scalar field system with $\mathbb s^3$ topology, for any scalar field mass $\mathfrak{m}\geq 0$, that lead to the formation of an exactly extremal schwarzschild-de sitter black hole in finite time, and that moreover the apparent horizon of the solution is exactly isometric to that of the subextremal schwarzschild-de sitter solution at earlier times. we also show that if the scalar field mass satisfies $\mathfrak{m}>\sqrtλ/2$, an analogous result holds having the extremal schwarzschild-de sitter white hole or the nariai solution in place of the black hole. in the black hole case, the exactly extremal schwarzschild-de sitter region is bounded to the future by two event horizons and can be seen as the analogue of the exterior region in the asymptotically flat case. we moreover establish that these two black hole horizons that bound the exactly extremal schwarzschild-de sitter region are the only event horizons present in the spacetime, something non-trivial given the existence of multi-black hole configurations when $λ> 0$. consequently, the solutions arising from these data can be thought to constitute, in particular, regular counterexamples to the third law of black hole thermodynamics with $λ>0$ arising from the collapse of physically plausible matter which is moreover uncharged. our approach to construct the cauchy data relies on $c^k$ characteristic gluing results for the einstein-scalar field system in spherical symmetry, in the spirit of [ku25].

title: curvature inequalities and rigidity for constant mean curvature and spacetime constant mean curvature surfaces
abstract: we establish curvature inequalities and rigidity results for constant mean curvature (cmc) surfaces in riemannian manifolds and spacetime constant mean curvature (stcmc) surfaces in lorentzian manifolds. in three-dimensional riemannian manifolds with nonnegative scalar curvature, we show that the christodoulou-yau inequality $h^2\leq 16π/|σ|$ ($h$ denoting mean curvature and $|σ|$ area) for stable cmc spheres also holds for cmc surfaces of arbitrary topology under a new stability condition controlling only the constant mode of the second variation of area. under an extrinsic curvature sign condition, equality forces the enclosed region to be euclidean without additional intrinsic assumptions. we extend these results to higher dimensions and to the hyperbolic and spherical settings.   in the lorentzian setting, we develop a variational stability theory for stcmc surfaces based on the second variation of area in the mean curvature vector direction. we introduce two independent stability notions: variational stability, which recovers classical volume-preserving cmc stability for surfaces in totally geodesic spacelike hypersurfaces, and constant-mode stability. under the dominant energy condition, either yields the sharp inequality $|\vec h|^2\leq 16π/|σ|$. in the equality case, under suitable geometric assumptions, the maximal globally hyperbolic development of the enclosed spacelike region is a minkowski causal diamond. these results imply nonnegativity and rigidity of the hawking quasi-local energy for stable stcmc surfaces. finally, we analyze known spacelike and null stcmc foliations, showing that asymptotic leaves are stable under positive mass conditions, whereas the local matter density and trace-free extrinsic curvature govern the instability of local foliations.

title: the dirac equation in arbitrary coordinate systems and curved spacetimes - an orthonormal frames approach
abstract: in this pedagogical article we discuss the dirac equation in arbitrary coordinate systems. we explain the need for connections when dealing with spinor fields and present the practical steps needed to compute the dirac operator in a general setting, allowing for arbitrary coordinate systems and position-dependent orthonormal gamma matrices, both of which can simplify computations in certain scenarios. the extension to include minimally coupled gravity is straightforward. examples are provided, including constructing the dirac equation in spherical and cylindrical symmetry (with or without gravity) and the kerr spacetime. we also briefly comment on the advantages and disadvantages of various tetrads and orthonormal gamma matrices. this manuscript should be accessible to readers who have studied the dirac equation at an introductory level (e.g., in cartesian coordinates in flat spacetime with constant gamma matrices). the emphasis is on the use of orthonormal frames, since these correspond to the coordinate systems most familiar to readers when dealing with most field theories, and represent the physical frames where measurements are performed. the aim is to get the reader quickly to the point of being able to do calculations, so the presentation favors a concise, pragmatic approach over extended derivations.

title: cosmological rigidity in $3$ spacetime dimensions
abstract: we establish rigidity theorems for cosmological spacetimes in $3$ spacetime dimensions. in the setting of the bartnik splitting conjecture, under the additional assumptions of null geodesic completeness and the dominant energy condition, we show that the spatial topology is either spherical or the spacetime splits as a product. our methods rely on the theory of marginally outer trapped surfaces, known rigidity results in the presence of a timelike or null line, and more recent rigidity results in the context of penrose's singularity theorem due to the first two authors, from which the existence of a foliation by totally geodesic null hypersurfaces can be concluded. our second main result closes the argument by establishing a splitting theorem for cosmological and null geodesically complete $3$-dimensional spacetimes which satisfy the dominant energy condition and which admit a foliation of the aforementioned type. in its proof, we make use of the local kundt structure of the metric and construct a global parallel generator for the null foliation.

title: an algebraic quantization of gravity from the null cone
abstract: we propose a background independent quantization of vacuum general relativity on four dimensional lorentzian spacetimes. starting from first order gravity, we solve the gravitational constraints on intersecting null cones of a bulk subregion and obtain the reduced phase space at finite $g_n$. we promote its canonical poisson brackets to commutation relations and use deformations of the reduced action to define an algebra of observables. equipped with this, we use gaussian wavefunctions of canonical pairs to construct a nonperturbative hilbert space representation, for which this algebra generates a type i factor. by composing amplitudes between states prepared on null cones, we then obtain a lorentzian path integral in which each sum over intermediate states converges absolutely. as a check, we compute the amplitude for graviton pair creation and annihilation on a null cone nonperturbatively in $g_n$ and find a finite closed form expression, even though expanding first in $g_n$ yields a logarithmic divergence. we next use diffeomorphism invariance of the path integral to show that a macroscopic causal diamond with a given maximum size has a finite dimensional hilbert space. from the lorentzian trace we obtain the bekenstein hawking entropy for marginally trapped surfaces and calculate its logarithmic correction for large schwarzschild black holes, recovering at one loop the coefficient sen obtained through euclidean methods. we end by deriving the semiclassical einstein equations to one loop as the low energy limit of this theory.

title: 1-laplacian type problems with strongly singular nonlinearities and gradient terms
abstract: we show optimal existence, nonexistence and regularity results for nonnegative solutions to dirichlet problems as $$ \begin{cases} \displaystyle -δ_1 u = g(u)|d u|+h(u)f & \text{in}\;ω,\\ u=0 & \text{on}\;\partialω, \end{cases} $$ where $ω$ is an open bounded subset of $\mathbb{r}^n$, $f\geq 0$ belongs to $l^n(ω)$, and $g$ and $h$ are continuous functions that may blow up at zero. as a noteworthy fact we show how a non-trivial interaction mechanism between the two nonlinearities $g$ and $h$ produces remarkable regularizing effects on the solutions. the sharpness of our main results is discussed through the use of appropriate explicit examples.

title: error estimates for a structure-preserving finite-element scheme of quasi-incompressible navier-stokes-maxwell-stefan systems
abstract: a conforming finite-element scheme for quasi-incompressible navier-stokes-maxwell-stefan systems in a bounded domain with periodic boundary conditions is presented. the system consists of the navier-stokes equations, together with a quasi-incompressibility constraint, coupled with the cross-diffusion maxwell--stefan equations. the numerical scheme preserves the partial masses and the quasi-incompressibility constraint and dissipates the discrete energy. first-order error estimates in space and time are shown for a diffusion-augmented mobility matrix by using the relative energy method and suitable projection error estimates. numerical experiments in two space dimensions illustrate the convergence of the scheme and indicate second-order convergence in space in the $l^2$ norm.

title: controlability of the 1d wave equation by point sources: outgoing states, circle rotations and small divisors
abstract: we characterise the states reachable from rest for the one-dimensional wave equation on the real line driven by finitely many fixed point sources. the characterisation reduces the control problem to a cohomological equation on a circle whose length is twice the distance between the outermost sources, with support constraints determined by the control time. for two sources, the reachable set is closed and the controls are unique at every finite time. for three sources, we give a complete classification in terms of the control time and the ratio of the two relevant travel times. below the time needed to traverse the outer interval twice, reachability is described by finite orbit sums. at and above this threshold, an irrational ratio produces a dense, non-closed reachable set in the compatible outgoing-state space, and exact reachability is determined by a small-divisor condition. we also quantify the cost of control. the minimum control norm is equivalent to the energy norm of the target plus a weighted fourier norm of its periodised defect. for a badly approximable irrational ratio, the worst cost for defects of fourier degree at most $n$ grows linearly in $n$, i.e. liouville ratios produce superpolynomial growth along subsequences. we derive constructive approximation estimates and sharp worst-case cost--accuracy rates on sobolev classes of defects. for an arbitrary number of sources, the long-time classification and the quantitative estimates are governed by simultaneous diophantine approximation of the source positions.

title: on the sharp vanishing order of the weyl tensor at a blow-up point for the yamabe equation in all dimensions
abstract: we determine the sharp vanishing order of the weyl tensor at a blow-up point of solutions to the yamabe equation in every dimension $n\ge 25$. on every closed, connected, smooth $n$-dimensional manifold $m$ of positive yamabe type and at any prescribed point $p\in m$, we construct a smooth metric $ \widehat g$ and a sequence of smooth positive solutions to the yamabe equation blowing up at $p$, such that the first nonzero covariant derivative of the weyl tensor at $p$ has any prescribed order $l$ satisfying $l\ge 6$ when $25\le n\le 29$, $l \ge 4$ when $30\le n\le 51$, and $l\ge 2$ when $n\ge 52$. moreover, $|\nabla_{ \widehat g}^{l}w_{ \widehat g}|>0$ everywhere on $m$.   earlier constructions realize every strictly higher order as the first nonzero order, while the known weyl vanishing results exclude every lower first nonzero order. thus the endpoint cases $l=6,4,2$ were the only ones left open, and are settled here. in particular, the order-two examples show that the compactness criterion $|w|+|\nabla w|>0$ is sharp.   at the endpoints, the construction arranges global and localized metric perturbations to interact at leading order in a limiting functional. for $l=2,4$, anisotropic polynomial ansatzes involving two orthogonal algebraic weyl tensors remove a distinguished translation degeneracy and produce $c^1$-stable saddle points. for $l=6$, a different polynomial ansatz produces a nondegenerate local minimum. higher prescribed orders are obtained by separating the perturbation that determines the limiting functional from the one that prescribes the weyl derivative.

title: critical exponent for nakao's problem in three space dimensions
abstract: we study a system consisting of a semilinear damped wave equation coupled to a semilinear wave equation in three space dimensions. we determine the sharp condition on the exponents of nonlinear terms that separates global existence for sufficiently small initial data from finite-time blow-up even for arbitrarily small data satisfying suitable positivity assumptions. to prove global existence, we combine a weighted pointwise estimate for the damped wave equation, which we established in earlier work, with a new one for the wave equation. the new pointwise estimate for the wave equation uses a combination of a parabolic weight and a light-cone weight. for the proof of blow-up, pointwise lower bounds are compared with integral upper bounds obtained by test functions. in the main estimates, explicit physical-space representations reveal how forcing near the wave cone influences the damped component on parabolic spatial scales and, in turn, the wave component inside the cone.

title: the sharp logarithmic loss in vanishing order for real planar schrödinger equations
abstract: we determine, up to constants, the largest possible order of vanishing of real solutions of $δu=vu$ in dimension two in terms of the size of the real potential~$v$. for each sufficiently large integer $k$, we construct a real potential $v\in c_c^\infty(b_1)$ with $\|v\|_\infty$ comparable to $k^2/\log k$ and a smooth real solution $u$ on $\r^2$ that vanishes to order $k$ at the origin, satisfies $\sup_{b_{1/2}}|u|=\|u\|_\infty=1$, and equals a positive constant outside~$b_{7/8}$. consequently, on every smooth connected closed riemannian surface, the largest order of vanishing at a prescribed point for real potentials of norm at most $m$ is comparable to $\sqrt{m\log m}$ for large~$m$, uniformly in the point. this gives a negative answer, in dimension two, to the square-root questions of kukavica and kenig. with the same building block, we also construct a nonzero real solution on $\r^2$ with $\|v\|_\infty\le1$ and $|u(x)|\le\exp(-c|x|\sqrt{\log|x|})$ for large~$|x|$, so that the landis conjecture fails in its exponential form in the plane even for real potentials. both constructions match the estimates of logunov, malinnikova, nadirashvili, and nazarov, which are therefore sharp.

title: scattering for the defocusing two-dimensional nls with an aharonov-bohm magnetic potential
abstract: we study the defocusing nonlinear schrödinger equation in two dimensions in the presence of an aharonov--bohm magnetic potential with noninteger flux. working with the friedrichs realization of the magnetic hamiltonian, we establish global well-posedness for initial data in the weighted magnetic energy space. for mass-critical and mass-supercritical nonlinearities, we prove convergence of the interaction representation in the same weighted space, while in the mass-subcritical range we obtain scattering in the magnetic energy space. the proof is based on a magnetic lens transformation, which converts the original equation into a nonlinear equation governed by the aharonov--bohm harmonic oscillator on a finite time interval. existence is obtained through truncation, compactness, and energy estimates, whereas uniqueness follows directly from the dispersive decay of the confined linear flow. this approach avoids derivative strichartz estimates, which are delicate in the presence of the singular magnetic field.

title: the capillary $l_{p}$ dual christoffel-minkowski-type problem for $p\geq q$ with $1\leq k\leq n$
abstract:
we study the following fully nonlinear $k$-hessian equation on a spherical cap $\mathcal{c}_θ$ for $1\leq k\leq n$ and $0<θ<π/2$: $$ \left\{  egin{aligned} σ_k(
abla^2h+hσ) &=fh^{p-1} igl(h^2+|
abla h|^2 igr)^{ rac{k+1-q}{2}} &&	ext{in }\mathcal{c}_θ,\ 
abla_μh&=\cotθ\,h &&	ext{on }\partial\mathcal{c}_θ. \end{aligned} ight. $$ under suitable convexity and boundary assumptions on $f$, we establish the existence of positive smooth strictly convex solutions for $p\geq q$, together with uniqueness when $p>q$ and $p\geq 1$. in the critical case $p=q>1$, scaling invariance prevents uniform $c^0$ estimates without normalization. we overcome this difficulty using a logarithmic gradient estimate and a normalized approximation with uniqueness up to dilation.

title: global well-posedness for the focusing gross-pitaevskii equation in the one-dimensional zhidkov space
abstract: we show global well-posedness for the focusing gross-pitaevskii equation in one spatial dimension, with initial data in the zhidkov space, with no smallness condition. for the usual nonlinear schrödinger equation with decaying initial data, a mass-energy argument is used to preclude finite-time blow-up. here both mass and total energy are infinite, but we put together a renormalized version of that bound by using the net mass transfer and the kinetic energy, which we show are a priori bounded. global well-posedness on the energy space and on $1+h^1$ follows. we also treat a variant of the equation with a smooth real density response to show how this construction can be generalized to different nonlinearities.

title: the singular paneitz equation on four-manifolds: refined blow-up analysis and degree jumps
abstract: we compute the leray--schauder degree of the singular paneitz equation on a closed four-manifold with conical orders strictly between minus one and zero. we assume that the kernel of the paneitz operator consists of the constants. in each positive nonresonant chamber the degree is a partial sum of an explicit generating series determined by the euler characteristic and the conical orders. we match the heights of exact blow-up solutions and expand the gradient near the corrected projected bubbles. a localized dilation identity gives its common-scale component on the zero set of the relative-scale equations. for generic data a fixed-mass homotopy then gives the signed degree of each concentrating configuration. assign ordinary points weight one and conical points weight one plus their order. if the largest concentrating weight exceeds one half, a finite second moment gives the coefficient. at one half the expansion acquires a logarithm, and below one half the coefficient is a global finite part. on the round four-sphere with two antipodal points of equal weight below one half, perturbing the prescribed curvature away from both points selects the side of bubbling.

title: oleinik estimate for a class of temple systems via vanishing viscosity limit
