abstract: in this article, we establish an oleinik type estimate for $2\times2$ systems of hyperbolic conservation laws in a class of temple systems via vanishing viscosity limit. more precisely, we consider the parabolic approximation with vanishing viscosity coefficient $\varepsilon u_{xx}$ ($\varepsilon>0$) for the temple class of hyperbolic system of conservation laws and for these approximate solutions we obtain an oleinik type estimate uniformly with respect to the viscosity coefficient $\varepsilon>0$. this extends the oleinik inequality for scalar conservation laws with viscosity to the system. subsequently, we prove that these approximate solutions converge via the process of vanishing viscosity limit to a global weak solution of the limit strictly hyperbolic system provided that the initial data is small in $l^\infty$. to do this we implement the vanishing viscosity method of bianchini and bressan [indiana univ. math. j. 2000] with $l^\infty$ initial data which requires new tools as an local in time oleinik estimate (obtained by employing a suitable maximum principle and a normal form argument) and a localization argument. in particular we need to introduce appropriate weight functions which satisfy a bellman equation to get new localized transversal interaction estimates.

title: strong ill-posedness for the surface quasi-geostrophic equations in $w^{k,1}(\mathbb{r}^2)$
abstract: we establish ill-posedness of the surface quasi-geostrophic equations in sobolev spaces $w^{k,1}(\mathbb{r}^2)$ for every integer $k \geq 3$. this includes the scaling critical space $w^{3,1}(\mathbb{r}^2)$. we build on ideas from (arxiv:2610.04872); in particular, we use a theorem of bonami and poornima to construct a basic building block, or packet, which obeys a linear evolution approximating that of the perturbation of the background solution to sqg. the bonami-poornima theorem ensures that this packet has both small initial $w^{k,1}$ norm and large $w^{k,1}$ norm at positive times. we then implement a process known as many packet dilution, which allows one to construct an initial perturbation as a sum of sufficiently many packets to dilute the effect of the nonlinear term. this initial perturbation leads to the desired norm inflation.   to establish instantaneous blow-up of the $w^{k,1}(\mathbb{r}^2)$ norm, we also prove a local well-posedness result in the critical sobolev-lorentz space $w^{2,(2,1)}(\mathbb{r}^2)$. this result gives a uniform lower bound on the existence time for solutions with bounded $w^{k,1}(\mathbb{r}^2)$ data, even though the solutions' $w^{k,1}(\mathbb{r}^2)$ norms may become arbitrarily large in arbitrarily short time.

title: acoustic gravitational waves from primordial curvature perturbations
abstract: standard perturbative calculations of scalar-induced gravitational waves (sigws) have neglected nonperturbative effects in the large-amplitude regime. we develop a hybrid numerical framework to signify nonperturbative effects on the stochastic gravitational wave (gw) background sourced by primordial curvature perturbations, focusing on the acoustic channel (fluid motions). fully general-relativistic, spherically symmetric simulations are used to extract nonperturbative sound-shell profiles from isolated curvature peaks; these profiles are then embedded into three-dimensional lattice evolutions of relativistic hydrodynamics coupled to transverse-traceless metric perturbations to compute the acoustic gw spectra. the acoustic signal has a peak frequency determined by the comoving shell thickness, and its amplitude is extremely sensitive to the mean comoving separation of peaks, scaling approximately as $r_{*c}^{-7}$. we find a robust causal low-frequency tail $\propto k^{3}$, and the nonlinear hydrodynamic interactions can enhance the ultraviolet power. comparing with sigws computed perturbatively from the same real-space configuration, we show that acoustic gws can be amplified by an order of magnitude and display a peak shifted to a lower frequency in the large-amplitude regime. these results highlight the importance of nonperturbative effects for accurate predictions of stochastic gw signals induced from primordial curvature perturbations.

title: reconstructed black hole solutions in the scalar-tensor theory with nonminimal coupling
abstract: we consider the scalar-tensor theory witn non-minimal coupling in the jordan frame. the action of the model contains a potential term $u(φ)$, a coupling function $f(φ)$. we explore a reconstruction procedure for a generic static spherically symmetric metric written in the buchdahl parametrization: $ds^2 = \left(a(u)\right)^{-1}du^2 - a(u)dt^2 + c(u)dω^2$, with given $a(u) > 0$ and $c(u) > 0$. the procedure gives the relations for $u(φ(u))$, $f(φ(u))$ and $dφ/du$, which lead to exact solutions to equations of motion with a given metric. a key role in this approach is played by the solutions to a first order linear differential equation for the function $f(φ(u))$. the formalism is illustrated by two examples when: a) the reissner-nordström-(anti-)de sitter metric and b) the bocharova-bronnikov-melnikov-bekenstein-(anti)de-sitter metric are chosen as a starting point.

title: self-force calculations with numerical relativity methods
abstract: to model gravitational waveforms from extreme mass-ratio inspirals (emris) for the upcoming lisa space mission, gravitational self-force calculations are needed to second order in perturbation theory. however, to date these calculations have only been attempted for the simplest case of circular orbits in schwarzschild spacetime. in this work, we present a new computational method aimed at performing generic second-order self-force calculations in kerr spacetime using methods from the adjacent field of numerical relativity. we perform an $m$-mode separation of variables, add null (``$vtu$'') slicing in horizon-penetrating coordinates, and solve the resulting elliptic partial differential equations using high-order discontinuous galerkin discretization, adaptive mesh refinement, and an iterative krylov-type linear solver with parallelizable multigrid-schwarz preconditioning. we find that our method achieves exponential convergence for the self-force on a scalar point charge in kerr spacetime up to spins of $|a|/m=0.998$ (thorne limit) on circular equatorial orbits as close as the innermost stable circular orbit (prograde and retrograde), despite the nonsmooth solution on the grid. we solve for 20 $m$-modes in parallel in a few seconds and retain the flexibility to extend the method to gravitational self-force and more generic orbits in the future. the code to perform these calculations is publicly available in the open-source numerical relativity code spectre.

title: the role of the volume in black hole thermodynamics
abstract: gibbons et al. [arxiv:hep-th/0408217] found the energy $e$ of kerr--anti-de sitter black holes by integrating the first law of black hole thermodynamics. they found that $e$ corresponds to the ashtekar--magnon--das (amd) energy associated with an asymptotically nonrotating frame, whereas the amd ``energy'' which i will call $f$ associated with an asymptotically rotating frame does not satisfy the first law. in cvetič et al. [arxiv:1012.2888], the first law was extended by interpreting $e$ as an enthalpy and $λ$ as being proportional to a pressure. the term conjugate to the pressure was then interpreted as the ``thermodynamic volume'' $v_{th}$. associated with the first law (with varying pressure) is a smarr relation for $e$. the smarr relation for $f$ also exists, and the term conjugate to the pressure in that smarr relation is the ``geometric volume'' $v_{geo}$, shown in [arxiv:1310.1935] to be equal to the vector volume $v_c$ of the black hole.   to address why it is necessary to use $e$ rather than $f$ to have a viable first law but $v_c$ appears naturally in the smarr relation associated with $f$ rather than $e$, i adapt barnich and compère [arxiv:gr-qc/0412029], by defining a conserved quantity $h^i_χ$ associated with killing vector $χ$. $e$ and $f$ are given by $h^i_ξ$ and $h^i_β$ respectively where $ξ$ is asymptotically hypersurface-orthogonal and $β$ is proportional to the divergence of the principal conformal killing--yano tensor $\boldsymbol{h}$. i show that the first law will be satisfied by $h^i_χ$ if both $χ^a$ and the background anti-de sitter metric have unvarying components, which holds for $ξ^a$ but not $β^a$, explaining why the first law works for $e$ but not $f$. i show that $v_c$ appears in the $β$-associated smarr relation due to simplifications related to $\boldsymbol{h}$.

title: ligo detector characterization in the second and third parts of the fourth observing run
abstract: ligo detector characterization efforts enabled the confident detection of gravitational waves from hundreds of compact binary coalescences during the fourth observing run. reliable production of high quality detector data and rapid noise mitigation efforts allow the extraction of the most in-depth knowledge of gravitational wave sources and their progenitors. in this paper we describe ligo detector characterization activities during the second and third parts of o4-o4b and o4c. we summarize changes in detector configuration and performance at the ligo hanford and ligo livingston observatories between the end of the first part of o4a and the end of o4c, including upgrades made during the commissioning break preceding o4b and during repairs performed in o4c. we describe instrumental investigations carried out at both sites designed to understand and subsequently mitigate the effect on detector sensitivity of transient glitches, narrowband spectral lines, and vibration-driven noise, among other data quality concerns. we then review the tools and procedures used to validate gravitational wave candidates and the data quality products thus supplied to searches for gravitational waves from compact binary coalescences and unmodeled transients, continuous gravitational waves, and the stochastic gravitational wave background. the efforts of the detector characterization group are essential for maintaining and improving the sensitivity and reliability of the ligo detectors especially as observing runs lengthen and more events are detected. we conclude with prospects for ligo detector characterization activities in future observing runs.

title: the black hole ir triangle for scalar qed
abstract: we construct the black hole infrared triangle of scalar qed on a stretched schwarzschild horizon at tree level. in the covariant phase space of the near-horizon maxwell field, the soft charge is a corner term. the memory is the zero mode of the gauge-invariant radiative field along the generators. it is conjugate to the boundary gauge mode that labels the degenerate horizon vacua, and gauss' law fixes it by the flux of charge through the horizon. the noether flux of the residual gauge transformation through the stretched horizon is not conserved by the scattering, because charged matter crosses the stretched horizon in both directions. the flux with its matter part removed is the soft charge, which generates the large gauge transformation. its ward identity is equivalent to a soft photon theorem in every radiative partial wave, which we derive from the near-horizon feynman rules and, where these do not control the emission, from the field equations at leading order. the main difference from null infinity is that on a stretched horizon both radial branches of the field are independent boundary data. the hard charge is a radial flux. with both branches present it weights each leg by the direction of its radial motion, and the soft factor is a sign per leg. the endpoint data on the two branches give two boundary observables, the time-integrated transverse magnetic and electric fields. the field radiated by a scattering process contributes only to the first, where it cancels the change in the coulomb memory of the charges, so that the soft charge is conserved. a charge that crosses the horizon enters both. we also discuss the infrared divergence, the dressing of the external states, and the fate of the memory in the hartle--hawking state, where it performs a random walk driven by the hawking radiation.

title: unitarization from spin geometry
abstract: we derive the dimensional reduction of 10d super yang-mills theory on a general closed 6d spin manifold using spectral decompositions for the higher-dimensional gauge field and gaugino, keeping the infinite towers of kaluza-klein (kk) modes in the lower-dimensional theory. we then calculate tree-level $2 \rightarrow 2$ scattering amplitudes with external massive spinors and vectors in this lower-dimensional theory. by studying the high-energy behavior of these amplitudes and imposing perturbative unitarity, we derive several sum rules that involve the eigenvalues of laplace and dirac operators on the internal 6-manifold, together with products of cubic coupling constants of the kk modes. these give concrete realizations of the known unitarity sum rules for spontaneously broken gauge theories. we illustrate explicitly how the simplest sum rule is satisfied for flat tori and round spheres.

title: bounds on love numbers and quasinormal modes from the surface impedance
abstract: the surface impedance of a body is fixed by its interior alone and encodes its entire tidal response. we derive bounds on love numbers and quasinormal modes from constraints on the impedance that follow from either of two properties of a stable body: it is lossless, meaning that it dissipates no energy, or it is passive, meaning that it never gives back more energy than it has received. for a lossless body, every dynamical love number is bounded from above and below, exactly in general relativity, in any renormalization scheme and at any scale. earlier bounds are exact for newtonian stars but fail for compact stars, because they take the response to arbitrarily fast tides to be zero or non-negative, whereas in general relativity it is negative. the quasinormal modes of a lossless body are also excluded from a region of the complex frequency plane set by the mass and radius. each known love number enlarges the excluded region. conversely, the quasinormal modes bound each love number from below, given the lower ones. for a passive body of horizon scale, such as a black hole, the static love number lies in a window that closes onto the vanishing black-hole value as the body's surface approaches the horizon.

title: chaotic singularities inside vacuum black holes
abstract: according to the conjecture of belinski, khalatnikov and lifshitz, general relativity gives rise to chaotic dynamics in the vicinity of generic spacelike singularities. however, no vacuum black hole has been shown to exhibit this behaviour. here we construct stationary, asymptotically locally ads$_5$ black holes with regular, triaxially squashed horizons and causal exteriors, whose homogeneous interiors realize the cosmological billiard of generic five-dimensional vacuum gravity. we identify a simple algebraic condition on the horizon data that is necessary for the interior billiard to be chaotic, and show that solutions with regular horizons locally access an open set of billiard trajectories.

title: quasinormal modes of black holes in astrophysical environments: rainbow in the dark matter
abstract: matter around black holes affects the ringdown in two ways: through the background geometry and through the response of the matter itself. we compute axial and polar gravitational quasinormal modes of a black hole embedded in a relativistic hernquist-type dark matter halo, following the fundamental mode and the first three overtones associated with the vacuum schwarzschild spectrum. the polar sector couples metric and matter perturbations. at small halo compactness, both sectors follow the familiar gravitational redshift law. most of the departure from the typical redshift at larger compactness is accounted for by the exact horizon lapse factor of the background. the remaining residual departure to this lapse is sector dependent. axial and polar frequencies are split, with their splitting growing from the fundamental through the third overtone. at large halo compactness the split grows by an order of magnitude, while overtone-to-fundamental frequency ratios depart from a common rescaling. within the adopted dark matter profile, the halo acts on the ringdown as a prism that disperses the gravitational spectrum, leaving a parity-dependent imprint that no common rescaling of the frequencies can reproduce. parity-isospectrality is, thus, broken.

title: hamiltonian approach to isospectrality in nonrotating black holes
abstract: in this work, we revisit the isospectrality of black hole perturbations from a hamiltonian perspective. for a nonrotating, uncharged system, we present a convenient canonical description of the background degrees of freedom that facilitates comparison with the usual lagrangian formulation. this allows us to identify phase-space counterparts of the superpotential and the algebraically special modes and show that they satisfy the expected isospectral relations, at least on shell or off shell modulo some subtle lapse redefinitions. finally, we investigate the extent to which these results persist in theories that effectively modify general relativity. in this setting, we formally quantify the corresponding deviations from the classical relations and the associated potential violations of isospectrality to first order in the modifications.

title: modular fluctuation relations on local causal horizons
abstract: local causal horizons provide a setting for studying horizon thermodynamics in the neighborhood of any regular spacetime point. here, we investigate this description beyond mean energy and entropy balances by studying fluctuations of boost-energy transfer induced by unitary perturbations of the horizon reference state. using the modular structure of the horizon algebra and a thermal reference state, we construct an energy transfer probability measure and derive integral and detailed fluctuation relations with the mean entropy production being expressed in terms of the araki relative entropy. the formulation accommodates type-iii algebras without introducing a reduced density matrix and can be extended to global bifurcate killing horizons admitting the required thermal reference state. for coherent scalar-field perturbations, we obtain a closed form for the characteristic function, identify the mean transfer with the excess boost-energy flux, and derive a thermodynamic uncertainty relation bounding the variance in terms of the mean transfer. we then explore the geometric implications by postulating a stochastic horizon entropy--area correspondence that associates an area change with each counted energy transfer. under this additional hypothesis, we obtain fluctuation relations for area changes and an area change uncertainty bound for coherent perturbations.

title: low-latency gravitational wave alert infrastructure and new data products for multi-messenger astronomy during ligo-virgo-kagra's fourth observing run
abstract: multi-messenger investigations of compact object mergers, such as binary neutron star and neutron star-black hole systems, remain among the most dynamic frontiers of modern astronomy. during the fourth observing run of advanced ligo, advanced virgo, and kagra, the search for joint electromagnetic and neutrino counterparts to gravitational-wave signals continued using public, semi-automated data products distributed in near real-time. the sky localizations and preliminary source characterizations provided by these alerts helped guide multiple rapid follow-up observations to candidate gravitational-wave events. during this run, the low-latency search parameter space was expanded to include the sub-solar mass regime and associated public data products were developed. further, chirp mass estimates of the binary merger system were introduced as a new public data product and distributed to enable follow-up searches to concentrate their resources on the most promising transients. in order to streamline the implementation of new searches and data products, a mock data challenge, known as the low-latency production integration challenge (llpic), was used as a replay of a simulated population of gravitational-wave sources to optimize and profile the software infrastructure and scientific deliverables. in this paper we describe these new public data products, their performance and the result of end-to-end testing of the low-latency infrastructure with the llpic.

title: environmental resonances in extreme-mass-ratio inspirals within boson clouds
abstract: extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (emris) offer a promising probe of matter environments around massive black holes through gravitational-wave (gw) observations. we investigate orbital resonances induced by conservative gravitational perturbations from such environments. combining a multiparameter expansion with the action-angle formalism, we derive a general resonance condition for generic bound kerr orbits. applying this framework to ultralight scalar clouds formed through black hole superradiance, we show that orbital resonances can arise from a single-mode cloud without requiring transitions between cloud modes. our analysis demonstrates that these resonances can lead to significant gw dephasing, providing a new avenue for probing boson clouds through gws and highlighting the importance of including environmental resonances in accurate emri waveform modeling.

title: holographic probes and krylov complexity on asymptotically lifshitz rotating black branes
abstract: we study two types of holographic probes on a five-dimensional, asymptotically lifshitz, rotating black hole. this geometry solves the field equations of einstein gravity coupled to a dilaton, two axionic scalars, and a maxwell doublet, supplemented by two vector doublets that enter the action through a parity-odd, chern-simons-like combination, as recently found in \cite{bravo-gaete:2026bdq}. this spacetime provides a concrete bottom-up arena to explore the imprints of rotation on probes in non-relativistic holography. first, we compute the holographic static quark-antiquark potential following the standard prescription that relates this boundary observable to the on shell-action of a string configuration whose endpoints are anchored at the boundary. we find that the screening length decreases both when the angular momentum is increased at fixed temperature and when the temperature is increased at fixed angular momentum. the former reflects centrifugal effects on the $q\bar{q}$ pair, whereas the latter stems from enhanced thermal fluctuations, which weaken correlations at a given separation. second, we compute the growth rate of the krylov complexity, using the holographic prescription that relates this observable to the momentum of a massive particle probe falling into the ir. in particular, we find that, at a given instant, the complexity grows faster as the dynamical exponent $z$ is increased.

title: cosmographic analysis of gravitational baryogenesis in running-$g$ cosmology
abstract: gravitational baryogenesis produces a baryon asymmetry through the coupling of the baryon current to the derivative of the ricci scalar, so its yield is set by the expansion history around decoupling. we study this mechanism in cosmology with a running newton coupling of the asymptotic-safety type. writing the ricci scalar and its derivative through the hubble rate, the deceleration parameter $q$ and the jerk $j$, we show that the yield is proportional to the kernel $k=2+q-j$, which vanishes for radiation in general relativity, and to a power of an enhancement factor measuring how strongly the running coupling accelerates the expansion at decoupling. we treat hybrid, intermediate, logamediate, emergent, bouncing and little-rip scale factors and determine where the observed asymmetry is reproduced for the $j^μ\partial_μr$ and $j^μ\partial_μr^2$ couplings; a table compares the six cases.

title: pinn-slicer: exploiting rotational symmetry to solve the photon orbit equation around a black hole
abstract: physics-informed neural networks (pinns) typically struggle with long-horizon domains, often requiring the network to be retrained as the domain grows. we present pinn-slicer, a method for second-order autonomous ordinary differential equations, $\ddot{u} = g(u, \dot{u})$, which exploits the invariance of this class of equations under translations of the independent variable. a single pinn, embedded within a solution ansatz that enforces the initial conditions explicitly, is trained on a thin slice of the independent variable using sobol-sampled initial conditions. the pinn is then deployed recursively, slice-by-slice, across the full domain. we demonstrate pinn-slicer on the nonlinear equation that describes photon orbits around a black hole, and reach a point-by-point root-mean-square error (rmse) below $10^{-3}$ in $u = r_s/r$ (the inverse radial coordinate in units of the schwarzschild radius) relative to a finite-difference reference solution. a key advantage of pinn-slicer is that a single trained network generalizes to any orbital initial condition within the training range, without retraining. in addition, pinn-slicer can cope with solution domains that may not be known a priori.

title: an electromagnetic ergoregion limits the reconnection-driven penrose process
abstract: magnetic reconnection taps black-hole rotational energy via negative-energy ejecta, but field geometry itself can forbid such ejection inside the spacetime ergoregion. we identify a covariant electromagnetic (em) ergoregion for general degenerate, magnetically dominated fields in stationary spacetimes. outside the em ergoregion, even ultrarelativistic field-guided ejecta cannot attain negative killing energy. for alfvénic reconnection outflows, the magnetization threshold scales inversely with the transverse distance to the em ergosurface. the mass-loaded kerr model places the em ergosurface at about 75% of the radial interval from the horizon to the spacetime ergosurface, close to the time-averaged boundary inferred from a dynamical simulation. together, these results show that field geometry determines where negative-energy ejection is possible, while magnetization sets the threshold for realizing it.

title: kiselev black hole from semiclassical gravity with conformal anomaly
abstract: investigating black hole physics in semi-classical gravitational theory is an interesting and important direction. when the backreaction of the conformal anomaly-induced effective stress-energy tensor is taken into account, the black hole spacetime can be largely altered which changes many properties of the black hole. in this work, rather than restricting our attention to the type-a anomaly, we incorporate the type-b anomaly and investigate how it modifies the spacetime structure obtained when only the type-a anomaly is considered. we find that for a specific relation between the central charges and the cosmological constant, the semiclassical einstein equations can be solved analytically, yielding a metric that takes the exact form of the kiselev black hole. after deriving the solution, we further discuss the properties of this new black hole solutions. our work serves as an essential stepping stone for studying black hole geometries under the full conformal anomaly.

title: the type-d accelerating taub-nut spacetime: construction, geometry and physical properties
abstract: we investigate the geometry and physical properties of the vacuum type-d accelerating taub--nut spacetime in the sector with vanishing kerr rotation. we recover its normalized metric from the plebański--demiański family and a dressed finite binary, tracking the horizon killing directions through the large-companion limit. the black-hole and acceleration horizons have distinct projective killing generators, and their intrinsic horizon geometry yields a relation between polar gaussian curvatures and cone angles that differs from that of the type-i accelerating taub--nut solution without requiring a matching of acceleration parameters. we establish separability of the type-d null hamilton--jacobi equation and construct an unwrapped radial conformal atlas with four simple-horizon extensions and five angular conformal diagrams. we also examine axial identifications and chronology-violating regions. the resulting geometrical and dynamical distinctions clarify how the two accelerating nut families differ despite sharing their nonaccelerating and zero-nut limits; the radial atlas is not claimed to be a unique maximal four-dimensional extension.

title: lorentz charges for lovelock gravity
abstract: in this paper, we construct the charges associated with the residual local lorentz transformations on a black hole horizon in the lovelock class of theories of gravity. the horizons is assumed to be non- expanding horizons, \emph{i.e} a null hypersurface for which the expansion corresponding to the null generator vanish. naturally, these hypersurfaces preserve only a subgroup of the full lorentz group of the bulk, and the residual symmetries correspond to the little group which stabilizes the horizon null generator. we show that on the horizon, the hamiltonian charge corresponding to the residual local lorentz boost is the wald entropy.

title: semiclassical causal geodesics: schwarzschild spacetime case
abstract: we propose an extension of the integral quantization, applied previously to the semiclassical description of a test particle in the flat minkowski spacetime, to the schwarzschild spacetime. this extension yields a local integral quantization. we calculate the transition amplitudes between coherent states of a particle in a mass layer, which effectively leads to a klein-gordon-type dynamics. the calculated probability distributions reproduce locally the classical radial geodesic motion in the schwarzschild spacetime. the local integral quantization presented here seems to be applicable to semiclassical quantization of geodesic motion in other curved spacetimes.

title: is gravitational-wave waveform systematics a bottleneck for formation channel inferences using effective-spin and mass-ratio?
abstract: gravitational-wave measurements of the effective spin $χ_\text{eff}$ and mass ratio $q$ help distinguish binary black hole formation channels, motivating a search for structure in the $χ_\text{eff} - q$ plane. however, both these quantities are known to be strongly correlated in gw parameter estimation since both enter the leading-order spin-orbit term together, and thus, the detectors cannot easily tell them apart. in this work, we harness the susceptibility of such measurements to waveform systematics by using injection-recovery studies with nrsur7dq4 as the true signal and seobnrv5phm and imrphenomtphm for parameter inferences. our study shows that, though there can be some parameter space in the $χ_\text{eff} - q$ plane, primarily in the unequal-mass regime, there can be some impacts from waveform systematics; overall, at a population level, the waveform systematics for the current detectors at their design sensitivity are not a bottleneck in recovering the underlying true population properties. we find that astrophysical properties such as $χ_\text{eff} - q$ correlations, which are signatures of different formation channels, are unlikely to be spuriously induced by waveform systematics, and inferences about formation channels based on such correlations are likely robust to waveform systematics at present, though some events that are in the parameter space of large impact can show some outlier behaviour. we find that some of the gw events such as gw190403$\_$051519 and gw240527$\_$230910 are in the vicinity of the $χ_\text{eff} - q$ parameter space, where large waveform systematics can arise, and these events are more susceptible to waveform systematics than others in gwtc-5. this study will play a vital role in precision astrophysical population inference from gw data in the future and in assessing the possibility of waveform systematics.

title: phenjax: the imrphenomt waveform family in jax for accelerated analyses on cpus and gpus
abstract: we present phenjax, a jax implementation of the precessing time-domain imrphenomt family of models for the gravitational wave signal emitted in compact binary coalescence. the code keeps the structure of its reference python implementation, phenomxpy, and reproduces, on average, its polarizations to a few $\times 10^{-12}$ of the peak strain for all the models, aligned-spin and precessing. the waveform models now take advantage of the jax construction: compiled once per array shape, vectorized over events (batching), differentiable and executed on cpus or gpus with the same source code. different additional features address the cost of long signals and of heterogeneous populations in a batch. on one nvidia h100, for the precessing tphm model on lisa-mass populations, phenjax is 3 to 6 times faster than phenomxpy when both codes evaluate one event at a time and 20 to 30 times faster when phenjax evaluates the events in batches of 8. we estimate that, for waveform generation, one gpu does the work of 1300 to 2700 cores of a current cpu node at 25 to 45 times less energy per waveform. as a backend of a global-fit lisa massive black hole pipeline, performed on the sangria dataset, phenjax recovers the same posteriors as the other waveform backends at a lower computational cost. in a comparison with phentax, the wall time was 13 minutes instead of 21.
